description.value: The study investigated changes in whole-brain functional connectivity associated with right inferior frontal cortex self-regulation training using real-time fMRI neurofeedback in adolescents with ADHD, and examined whether these changes were associated with clinical improvement and were specific to the trained region.

design.value: The original study was a randomized controlled trial testing the efficacy of fMRI-Neurofeedback of rIFC in 18 ADHD adolescents compared to 13 ADHD adolescents who had to enhance the left parahippocampal gyrus. The current study analysed functional connectivity changes from the first to the last neurofeedback run in the rIFC-Neurofeedback group and also reported the control group's changes to assess specificity.

task_description.value: Boys were offered 14 fMRI-Neurofeedback runs, 8.5 min each, in four 1–1.5 hr scan visits over 2 weeks. Each run consisted of seven rest blocks of 30 s and six activation blocks of 50 s. Participants attempted to move a rocket towards space by any means they found helpful while receiving continuous feedback every repetition time about BOLD activation in the target region.

presentation_software.value: custom fMRI-Neurofeedback interface system and a locally written program

instructions.value: You can try to concentrate on the rocket or try any other method that works for you.

stimuli.value: An underwater dolphin image during rest blocks and a video-clip of a rocket during activation blocks.

task_performance_measures.value: A score from 0–10 reflecting the percentage of distance travelled through space during each run
Distance travelled through space, with a monetary incentive corresponding to the best performance in the session

task_description.value: After the last fMRI-Neurofeedback run, a 5-min fMRI transfer run was conducted. It was identical to the Neurofeedback training runs and used the same stimuli, but without feedback, consisting of four rest and three activation blocks.

stimuli.value: The same underwater dolphin image and rocket video-clip as in the Neurofeedback training runs, but the rocket did not move.

Real-time fMRI processing included motion correction, creation of native-space masks for the selected ROI and white matter reference region, extraction of mean BOLD signals, and generation of continuous visual feedback.

steps.value: Define the target ROI in AFNI using the CA_N27_ML/TT_N template
Create native-space masks for the rIFC and white matter reference region
Extract the mean BOLD signal from each ROI for each newly acquired volume
Update the feedback threshold based on past performance

description.value: Offline fMRI data were processed using AFNI and XBAM; individual functional connectivity maps were transformed to standard Talairach space.

steps.value: Calculate a 3D volume containing the average intensity at each voxel over the whole experiment
Rigid-body realignment of each volume to the average-intensity template
Spatial smoothing with a Gaussian filter at 7.8 mm FWHM
Extract the average time series from each seed ROI in native space
Transform correlation maps by rigid-body transformation to the subject's high-resolution EPI and affine transformation to a Talairach template

model_settings.value: Pre- and post-fMRI-Neurofeedback effects on clinical measures, with group as the between-group factor and timepoint as the repeated within-subject factor.
Two-tailed Pearson correlations between post-treatment minus pre-treatment functional connectivity changes and post-treatment minus pre-treatment clinical outcome changes.
The average time series for each seed region was used as a model for a whole-brain correlation analysis producing functional connectivity maps.

Separate analyses tested positive and negative functional connectivity differences between the last (11th or earlier) and first fMRI-Neurofeedback run for Brodmann area 44 and Brodmann area 45 seed regions.
Tests of group differences in absolute and relative mean displacement.
Correlations between absolute and relative mean displacement values and significant functional connectivity changes in each group.
Run was the within-group repeated measure and group was the between-group measure; changes between the last and first run were compared between the rIFC-Neurofeedback and lPHG-Neurofeedback groups.
Direct group comparisons of the correlations between functional connectivity changes and clinical outcome changes.
